note: Memory-pressure ladders are driven through the guard's injected sample source, which is how a synthetic consumer is modelled deterministically. Cases that need a real kernel or a real Docker daemon are declared blockers.

blocked.reason: Needs a real kernel OOM kill. The guard's reaction to every pressure state, including emergency, is driven deterministically here through an injected sample source; what a kernel adds is that the PSI and available-memory signals move as modelled under a genuine OOM.
blocked.evidence_command: On a DGX Spark with a model loaded: sudo dmesg -w | grep -i 'killed process' in one shell, and a memory bomb (stress-ng --vm 8 --vm-bytes 90% --timeout 120s) in another, while curl -sS https://127.0.0.1:7443/api/v1/events streams
blocked.expected_evidence: dmesg records the OOM kill; the runtime emits memory.pressure.changed to emergency and inference.engine.stopped before the kill, and status reports memory_pressure=emergency then recovering.
